content.title: Brewers reward Miz with his first career Opening Day start
content.text: SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. – Jacob Misiorowski has been a top prospect and a rookie sensation. He rose to an All-Star Game faster than any player in history and fell into a second-half slump that cost him his spot in the Brewers’ rotation. Then he emerged as a bullpen ace in his first MLB postseason.Now you can add another experience for Milwaukee’s incarnation of Forrest Gump. Miz Trading Card Bobblehead Giveaway is April 11! The Brewers announced they will hand the ball to 23-year-old Misiorowski for their season opener against the White Sox at American Family Field on Thursday – an appropriate pick for a team heading into the regular season with a group of starters long on promise but short on experience. Misiorowski will match up against White Sox right-hander (and former Minor League teammate) Shane Smith at 1:10 p.m. CT.“I don’t think there’s such a thing as too amped up,” Misiorowski said after pitching parts of five innings in the Brewers’ 8-7 loss to the D-backs on Friday night in his final spring tuneup. “I want all the juices I possibly can get. So I’m excited for it.”“I’ve always had that,” he said. “I’ve always needed [it]. The more juice, the better.”Milwaukee won’t have right-hander Quinn Priester, who is bound for the injured list with symptoms of thoracic outlet syndrome, and won’t have Brandon Woodruff, who is healthy but will either begin the regular season on the back end of the rotation or on the IL as he builds his pitch count cautiously, coming off a series of injury-shortened seasons. How Misiorowski compares to other young Brewers Opening Day starters If Brewers officials harbored any last-minute hope that Woodruff, back with the team after accepting a qualifying offer to earn the highest single-season salary for a pitcher in franchise history, would demand the ball for what would have been a third Opening Day start, that ended when he surrendered a pair of home runs with a fastball dipping below 90 mph during his fourth inning on the mound against the Rangers on Thursday night.“He’s a nice young talent,” said Murphy, who didn’t announce any rotation plans beyond Misiorowski getting the opener. “He gave us great hope with the way he finished the season and came into camp. We think it’s a good way to get going.“Obviously, if Woody is 100%, Woody would be in that spot. Traditionally, people like Woody – he’s our one veteran starter. But ‘Miz’ is going to step up.”Murphy was not ready to say whether Woodruff would open the season in the back of the opening rotation or with a backdated stint on the injured list. Either way, he is expected to join the Brewers' rotation in early April.Other pitchers expected to start games for Milwaukee early in the year include right-handers Chad Patrick and Brandon Sproat and left-hander Kyle Harrison. Lefty Robert Gasser is another candidate, and the Brewers are pondering employing at least one opener on the first homestand against the White Sox and Rays. Aaron Ashby is the leading contender for that assignment."I think we're going to have to be creative on our pitching staff," Murphy said. "But we've done that before. Miz being the Opening Day choice, I think he's very capable."The Brewers have never had a starting pitcher like him, and there never was a rookie season in Milwaukee like his, when Misiorowski went 5-3 with a 4.35 ERA in 14 starts plus one relief appearance. Those final numbers obscure the way his career began: He didn’t allow a baserunner until his 13th inning on the mound in the Majors against the Cardinals and Twins, then posted victories opposite a pitcher on his way to winning the 2025 National League Cy Young Award, Paul Skenes of the Pirates, and another pitcher headed to the Hall of Fame, Clayton Kershaw of the Dodgers.Misiorowski made the NL All-Star team after five big league starts, besting Skenes (11 starts in 2024) for the earliest invitation in history.The second half wasn’t the same. Maybe it was the extended rest built into his schedule. Maybe it was the comebacker off his left shin in his final start of July, and a short stint on the injured list. Maybe it was the fact he was facing Major League hitters working off Major League scouting reports.Whatever it was, Misiorowski posted a 5.45 ERA in nine starts after the break and was removed from the rotation. After one relief appearance against the Reds during the final weekend of the regular season, the Brewers trusted Misiorowski’s makeup and velocity enough that they included him on the roster for the NL Division Series against the Cubs and the NL Championship Series against the Dodgers, and he delivered electric multi-inning appearances in both.That propelled him into the offseason, Misiorowski said, with a shot of confidence.“You never know what you’re going to see,” said first baseman Jake Bauers, who backed Misiorowski on Friday night by hitting his fifth home run of the spring. “I’m excited to see him in that environment. I know his juices will be flowing on the mound. He likes to get fired up.”Misiorowski is just as fired up to see the pitchers who follow him – even though the Brewers haven’t yet revealed who they will be, and in what order they will roll out.“I think we’ll be fun to watch,” Misiorowski said. “All of our guys are just fun. It’s exciting to see. The new guys coming in that we got this offseason are looking really good.”As he handed the baseball to his manager and left the mound in the fifth inning, with 86 pitches in the bank and two outs, Misiorowski was laughing.“Because when I walked out to take him out,” Murphy said, “he didn’t want to come out. I said, ‘Don’t start this stuff!’”On Thursday, it starts for real.Supervising Club Reporter Adam McCalvy has covered the Brewers for MLB.com since 2001.Skenes back to Cy Young form in win after tough Opening Day start7:33 PM UTCCINCINNATI -- Pirates ace Paul Skenes rebounded from the shortest outing of his career to post five strong innings Wednesday and earn his first win of the season, 8-3, against Cincinnati at Great American Ball Park.After allowing five runs on four hits, walking two and hitting a batter while retiring just two batters last Thursday, Skenes (1-1) allowed just one run on three hits, striking out five and walking two. He tossed 77 pitches (51 strikes) and lowered his season ERA from 67.50 to 9.53. Skenes left with a 4-1 lead thanks to an Oneil Cruz three-run homer off Cincinnati starter Andrew Abbott (0-1) in the first. Pirates Home Opener is Friday vs. the Orioles -- Get your tickets now! Mason Montgomery relieved Skenes to start the sixth, and allowed a pinch-hit two-run homer to Eugenio Suárez as the Reds cut the Pirates’ lead to one run. But Isaac Mattson, Justin Lawrence and Gregory Soto finished off the final 3 1/3 innings for Pittsburgh’s first series victory of the season.The Pirates have Thursday off before their home opener Friday afternoon against Baltimore.Bryan Reynolds blasted a two-run homer deep to the seats in right in a four-run ninth for his 140th as a Pirate, moving him into sole possession of ninth place all-time in Pirates history.Skenes didn’t give up a hit until Elly De La Cruz swatted a 90.1 mph changeup to right field for a single to open the bottom of the fourth. After Sal Stewart’s grounder moved De La Cruz to second, Nathaniel Lowe doubled him home, snapping Skenes’ scoreless streak against Cincinnati at 31 innings, dating to his first career start against the Reds on June 17, 2024.Coming into Wednesday’s game, the opponent figured to be the perfect elixir for the flame-throwing Pittsburgh ace after his shortest career outing six days earlier against the Mets in Queens.In five previous starts against the Reds, Skenes was 4-0 with a 0.31 ERA, covering 29 innings. He struck out 40 and walked just two batters. Skenes had not allowed a run against Cincinnati since the first inning of his first start against the Reds.Like his Opening Day start last Thursday, Skenes had an early lead to work with, this time thanks to Cruz belting his third homer of the series and season, and his second in as many at-bats.With two outs, Reynolds singled and Marcell Ozuna walked. Cruz then hopped all over a hanging curve from Abbott and unloaded it a Statcast-projected 407 feet to right for a 3-0 Pirates lead in the first.Skenes needed a batter to find his rhythm, walking leadoff man TJ Friedl on five pitches. But unlike his outing against the Mets, he quickly found a groove, striking out Matt McLain and De La Cruz before retiring the red-hot Stewart on a force out at second.
